thread:
Priya: Quick sync — proposing an "Isolation Pledge" initiative for Q4. Goal: a clear, customer-facing set of routing policies + tenant fencing primitives so sales/customers can buy with predictable SLAs and residency guarantees. High level: policy DSL, routing fabric, rollout gates, and launch criteria. Asking: what do we need to call this minimally shippable?
Sam: +1. Can you list the absolute must-haves vs nice-to-haves? i.e., is KMS + per-tenant egress enough initially, or do we need per-tenant GPU pools?
Priya: Must-haves I see: documented policy DSL, enforcement at routing layer (soft isolation), basic residency tagging, SLA definition (latency targets + eviction rules), and a cutover playbook. Nice-to-haves: dedicated GPU pools, per-tenant billing attribution, advanced evict/soft-evict UI.
Leo: Engineering notes: soft isolation (routing preference + affinity) is straightforward. Strong isolation (dedicated pools) is an ops+capacity problem. Prefetch/KV cache semantics make strict eviction trickier — KV caches are global unless we bind cache keys to tenant namespaces. That has perf implications.
Jordan: From product/CS: customers asking for a contractual "fencing" promise — they want an onboarding checklist and acceptance test. Can we define a 5-step acceptance test they can run?
Priya: Idea for acceptance test (minimal): 1) Deploy model with tenant tag and residency flag. 2) Route synthetic traffic from tenant X -> verify routing path respects residency. 3) Assert latency < target for 95th perc. 4) Trigger simulated node loss -> verify fallback policy respects tenant SLA. 5) Validate logs/audit entries + KMS key access.
Sam: Need measurable metrics to gate launch: p95 latency, cold-start rate, percent of requests served from local region, tenant isolation incidents (0), and cost delta vs baseline. Can we top-line targets?
Leo: Proposed gates: p95 <= 250ms for typical gen workloads; cold-starts < 2% at baseline load; region-local >= 95% for residency-tagged traffic. Ops needs rollback hooks: automatic fallback to compatible model variant + traffic drain.
Priya: Dependencies: routing policy DSL (product + eng), telemetry additions (per-tenant tracing), audit/KMS work (security), rollout playbook (SRE), and demo customers for pilot. Timeline ask: pilot in 10 weeks if we scope must-haves tightly.
Jordan: Pilots — nominate 2 customers with clear residency needs. We should prepare an NDA-friendly runbook and a small SLA addendum. Also prepare a risk register: capacity, egress costs, legal/regulatory.
Leo: Implementation notes: prefer feature-flagged rollout. Start with: 1) read-only policy UI + dry-run routing logs; 2) soft-enforce routing (preference) for pilot; 3) full enforcement + quota isolation later. This reduces blast radius.
Sam: UX ask: product needs an exportable Acceptance PDF and a short checklist for sales. Also a one-pager on economic impact (expected cost uplift vs premium pricing).
Priya: For launch criteria checklist (draft): - Policy DSL 1.0 stable + docs; - Telemetry: per-tenant traces & cost attribution; - Pilot with 2 customers completed; - Rollout playbook + rollback; - Legal sign-off on residency claims; - Post-launch 30-day monitoring dashboard.
Jordan: Who owns each bullet? Priya: product owner. Leo: eng owns DSL + telemetry. Sam: growth owns sales materials. SRE owns rollout. Legal/security to sign. Can we put owners in the tracker?
Priya: I'll spin up a GH tracking board today and tag owners.
deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: infra/feature-flagging-branch -> staging at 2025-03-10T15:00Z :rocket:
Sam: Tiny suggestion — include an experiment to measure economic break-even for customers (cost vs latency tradeoff) as part of pilot. If we can show unit economics, sales will be easier.
Leo: Agreed. For experiments we'll add a toggled quantization profile + batching knobs to the pilot config to measure cost/latency curves.
Priya: OK action items: 1) Priya create GH board + draft acceptance PDF; 2) Leo prototype policy DSL and dry-run router by week 2; 3) Sam line up 2 pilot customers; 4) Jordan coordinate legal/security checks; 5) SRE prepare canary playbook. Will post owner assignments.
Sam: cool. Thanks — will prep customer comms once we have the acceptance doc.
Jordan: Putting this on next Wednesday's product/arch sync for a final go/no-go.
Priya: Thanks team. Expect the GH board link in ~1h. :thumbsup:
